scenes.name: what a branch means in lockstep
scenes.visual: A thirty-two-lane warp encounters an if-else decision in code. Sixteen lanes want the 'if' path; sixteen want the 'else' path. The hardware cannot run both at once, so it executes them sequentially in two passes, masking out half the lanes in each pass.

beats.say: On an ordinary processor, a conditional branch is routine. One thread reaches a decision, takes one path, and carries on.
beats.show: A single CPU thread reaches a fork in code: 'if x > 0'. It takes the right path cleanly with zero wasted cycles.

beats.say: On a G P U, thirty-two lanes reach that fork together sharing one instruction, but the numbers they are testing differ in every lane.
beats.show: A 32-lane warp approaches the fork. Half the lanes evaluate to true; the other half evaluate to false. Two conflicting instruction paths highlight in violet and amber.

beats.say: There is only one instruction decoder, so the hardware cannot run both branches at once. It runs them back to back, masking off half the lanes in each pass.
beats.show: Pass 1: the 'if' path executes. Lanes 16 through 31 are greyed out as idle. Pass 2: the 'else' path executes. Lanes 0 through 15 are greyed out as idle.

beats.say: Each lane sits completely idle through the half it skipped. A balanced if-else branch cuts throughput in half.
beats.show: A throughput meter drops from 100% to 50%. Takeaway: 'warp divergence: divergent paths are serialized, not parallelized'.

scenes.name: the active mask and nested forks
scenes.visual: The hardware active mask displayed as a 32-bit register. A bar chart demonstrates the exponential penalty of nested branches: each additional nested condition doubles the number of serial passes and halves efficiency.

beats.say: The hardware enforces divergence using an active bitmask: one bit for each of the thirty-two lanes.
beats.show: A 32-bit register card displays: 'Active mask: 11110000...'. The ones execute; the zeros simply discard their outputs.

beats.say: Inactive lanes still occupy their place in the execution slot. They simply discard the result.
beats.show: Instruction slots pulse across the lanes. Inactive lanes drop their results into a grey waste bin.

beats.say: Each nested fork doubles the passes: one fork means two passes; two nested forks mean four passes; three nested forks mean eight passes.
beats.show: A tree of nested if-else blocks branches downward. Efficiency bars drop precipitously: 1 pass is 100%, 2 passes is 50%, 4 passes is 25%, 8 passes is 12.5%.

beats.say: A branch costs nothing when all thirty-two lanes take the same path. Divergence only happens when lanes disagree.
beats.show: When all lanes evaluate true, the entire warp takes the branch in one pass at 100% efficiency. Takeaway pill: 'branching is free when warps agree; data-dependent splits destroy efficiency'.

scenes.name: the two cardinal sins
scenes.visual: A side-by-side conceptual comparison of the GPU's two cardinal sins: Divergence on the left, Uncoalesced Memory Access on the right. Both stem from the exact same structural cause: thirty-two lanes forced to act as one.

beats.say: Divergence is the first of two cardinal sins in G P U programming. The second is uncoalesced memory access.
beats.show: Two large caution panels appear: left 'Divergence (Instruction mismatch)', right 'Uncoalesced access (Address mismatch)'.

beats.say: Both sins have the exact same cause: thirty-two lanes that are bound together by hardware to act as one.
beats.show: A blue warp bracket binds 32 lanes at center. Arrows connect the bracket to both caution panels.

beats.say: Divergence happens when lanes want different instructions, wasting arithmetic issue slots.
beats.show: In the left panel, lanes branch in different directions, leaving half the issue slots grey and wasted.

beats.say: Uncoalesced access happens when lanes want scattered memory addresses, wasting memory bandwidth. And bandwidth is by far the scarcer resource.
beats.show: In the right panel, lanes point at scattered memory addresses, forcing multiple separate memory transactions. Takeaway: 'a group that acts as one must agree on instructions and on addresses alike'.
